title: Choose the visual world for the ProofFeed landing page
question: The roll assigned Station Record. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Station Record
options.lineage: seismograph drum charts and instrument chart recorders
options.thesis: A price feed is an instrument, not a claim. You cannot draw on the paper yourself: the pen is driven by the ground, exactly as no setPrice exists and every value is driven by a proven mainnet transaction. USDC ran flat at a dollar for years and then, on 2023-03-11, the pen swung to $0.88.
options.viewport: The 2023-03-11 depeg owns the whole first screen as one instrument record: a ruled time base, the USDC trace flat at 1.00000000 then dropping to 0.88000000, the event annotated in red pencil the way a station operator marks a chart, and a station block naming the source chain, the block height and both transaction hashes.
options.risk: A chart implies continuity. This feed is explicitly a lower bound with gaps, so the trace must render gaps as gaps or the world would tell exactly the lie the README spends a section correcting.

raised.raise: Ballistic honesty: the trace plots only proven rounds at true time spacing, and unproven intervals render as gaps rather than a smoothed line the product cannot claim.
The notation is the stage: the real AnswerUpdated topic hash and the decoded log fields are primary content, not prose describing them.
The time grid never stretches. It re-counts columns per viewport and holds one tick rhythm at every width.
The 2023 record is a complete reading in the first viewport, not a hero teaser with the substance below the fold.
Provenance rides beside the value: chain key, block height, transaction index and gas sit next to every number, never in a footnote.
On phones the trace, its annotations and its values unroll as synchronized lanes that stay time-aligned instead of reflowing independently.

options.label: The Tape
options.lineage: ticker tape and ruled ledger columns
options.thesis: The feed as a running financial tape: monospace figures in ruled columns, each proven round a line, the depeg the line that breaks the run.
options.viewport: A single ruled column of proven rounds, newest first, with the 2023 line pulled out and enlarged.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on, and the one my own ranking put first. Familiar and safe; a judge has seen this page before.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.viewport: A row of needles, one per feed, leaning into the red together.
options.case: Loses both axes. A VU meter asserts a live present value, which is precisely what this feed cannot prove; the metaphor would contradict the product's central limitation. Audio gear is also not this audience's working world.
options.risk: Would read as claiming real-time data.

options.label: Algorave Source Floor
options.viewport: One code buffer at stage scale, the cursor line as the downbeat.
options.case: Loses both axes. The product proves a past event, while a live-coding grammar is about edits taking effect on the next cycle. Developers would identify with it; judges would not.
options.risk: Neon on black is the exact rut this project should avoid.

options.label: Wiener Werkstatte Gridsmith
options.viewport: Content held inside square-punched lattice frames.
options.case: Loses both axes for this audience. The lattice holds tabular data well but expresses neither proof nor time, and its nested-casket topology runs straight into the user's ban on nested containers.
options.risk: Nested frames are the banned pattern wearing couture.

options.label: Vertical Feed Surface
options.viewport: One item filling the viewport, action glyphs on the right rail.
options.case: Loses both axes. Judges must compare an Etherscan value against a Blockscout value, and a grammar built to show one complete item at a time actively prevents comparison. It also needs full-bleed media this project does not have.
options.risk: Entertainment grammar on an evidence page.

options.label: Fracture Glaze Shelf
options.viewport: A row of glaze samples, gravity setting the reading order.
options.case: Loses both axes. Ceramics is far from this audience's working world, and flow-arrest-pool has no honest mapping onto cryptographic verification.
options.risk: Metaphor with no load-bearing connection to the mechanism.

options.label: Rain-Night Cityscape
options.viewport: Skyline, street canyon and river reflection as synchronized night bands.
options.case: Loses both axes, and is disqualified besides: cobalt-and-neon with wet reflections is the crypto-landing-page rut the brief explicitly bans, glow included.
options.risk: Directly violates the user's stated constraint.

canonCard.label: The Category Standard
canonCard.thesis: Near-black ground, one neon accent, a hero claim about trustless infrastructure, three feature cards, a gradient glow behind the fold.
canonCard.viewport: Centered hero claim, subhead, two buttons, three feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Played straight it is competent and instantly legible to a judge. It is also the page the user named as the thing to avoid, and it would make this project look like every other submission.
